title: Unramified morphisms descend along affine-transition limits
statement: Let $I$ be a nonempty directed set and $(S_i)_{i\in I}$ an inverse system of quasi-compact quasi-separated schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions] with affine transition morphisms [pqf-def-affine-morphism] and limit $S$ [lem-weil-pbc-limit-affine-transition]. Fix $i_0\in I$, quasi-compact quasi-separated $S_{i_0}$-schemes $U_0,V_0$, and an $S_{i_0}$-morphism $g_0:U_0\to V_0$. For $i\geq i_0$ put $U_i=U_0\times_{S_{i_0}}S_i$, $V_i=V_0\times_{S_{i_0}}S_i$, and let $g_i:U_i\to V_i$ be the induced morphism; define $g:U\to V$ similarly over $S$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. Assume $g_0$ is locally of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] and $g$ is unramified [def-weil-unramified-morphism]. Then there exists $i\geq i_0$ such that $g_i$ is unramified. No flatness, finite presentation or Noetherian assumption on $g_0$ is required.
